neighbours.label: falling asleep / napping (nap, dozed, drowsy, asleep)
fire: After the long drive, Grandpa stretched out on the sofa for a quick nap.
The heat in the lecture hall made half the students drowsy by noon.
She dozed off halfway through the second act of the opera.
The puppy was fast asleep in its basket before the guests arrived.
On Sunday afternoons my father always naps in his armchair.
The cold medicine left him so drowsy that he skipped his shift.
I nodded off on the train and missed my stop.
The toddler finally fell asleep in the car seat.
quiet: After the long drive, Grandpa stretched out on the sofa to read the paper.
The heat in the lecture hall made half the students fan themselves by noon.
She checked her phone halfway through the second act of the opera.
The puppy was chewing a toy in its basket before the guests arrived.
On Sunday afternoons my father always reads in his armchair.
The cold medicine left him so hoarse that he skipped his shift.
I looked out of the window on the train and counted the stops.
The toddler finally stopped crying in the car seat.

notes: Card: nap x4, d|rows|iness x5, do|zed x4, asleep x3, Russian с|он; output promotes sleep, sleeping, dreams. The - pole is bedtime-but-awake context (sit, book, by myself). Near misses keep the same scenes with the person awake.
